_readme: NEXUS tenant-precedence three-dealer fixture (A/B/C). Consumed by setup.py,
journeys.py and teardown.py in this directory -- edit this file, not the
scripts, to change who/what gets created.
OWNER TODO: every contact point below is a plus-addressed alias of
aliasgher892@gmail.com so all test mail/WhatsApp lands in one inbox during
development. Swap in your own 4 real mailboxes (one per dealer member user
A/B/C plus a spare) before handing this fixture to anyone else -- search
this file for 'aliasgher892' to find every place that needs changing.
PHONES: deliberately only two real-looking numbers are used anywhere in
this fixture -- PHONE_DUBAI and PHONE_INDIA below -- reused on purpose:
* c2 uses PHONE_INDIA in EVERY dealer (A, B and C) -- cross-tenant
identity-collision probe: the same phone number reaching three
different dealerships must resolve to three separate, tenant-scoped
rows, never a merge and never a cross-tenant read.
* c1 and c3 within the SAME dealer both use PHONE_DUBAI, but with two
different emails (a household/shared-number case) -- same-dealer,
non-dedupe probe: leads.leads_tenant_email_key is UNIQUE(tenant_id,
email), not phone, so two different people who share a phone number
must file as two separate rows, not get merged into one.
* c4 uses PHONE_INDIA and is marked dedupe_probe=true -- journeys.py
pushes c4's exact payload (same email, same marker) through the lead
door TWICE to prove the (tenant_id, email) upsert on_conflict target
dedupes to exactly one row instead of creating a duplicate.
See supabase/migrations/20260902102629_mt_keys_scope_natural_keys_to_tenant.sql
and .../20260902112540_mt_keys_drop_leads_email_global_unique.sql for the
schema decision this fixture is built to exercise.
Dealer A is NOT a test tenant -- it is the real, existing Tenant A tenant
(fff6a2b5-cfd5-4460-8383-875bc5826de0). setup.py never creates or deletes
that tenant; it only ensures a test MEMBER user + membership on it, same as
the existing dealer-b two-tenant script already did. journeys.py therefore
writes real NEXUS-TEST rows into the production Tenant A tenant -- they are
all marked and all removable by teardown.py, but they are not sandboxed.
